Pack 20 to 60 heads, cabbages and turnips in any mix, with up to one apple and one carrot for every five heads if you like, then salt and compress it under a cloth, a plank and a flat stone.
Until it is salted and compressed you can still unpack everything. Once it is, nothing more goes in.
About 4 weeks at 18°C, 6 at 13°C, 2 to 3 when warm, 2 to 4 months in the cold; stopped at 0°C. Above 27°C for 2 days it goes soft and keeps only 2/3 as long; for 5 it spoils.
Take it out a portion at a time. It keeps about 6 months in a cellar, a month in a warm room. The last portion gives the plank and stone back.
Empty it to get the plank and stone back.
Salts the kraut and presses it down under the cloth, the board and the stone, so its own juice rises over it as brine. The barrel is sealed and the kraut starts to sour: nothing more goes in.
